title: NHL free agent big board 5.0: Expanding to 100 top targets a day before the frenzy
content:
Let the bidding begin!

Even as NHL teams prepare for Wednesday’s opening bell on a free-agent market that doesn’t include a true headliner or game-breaker, they do so knowing it’s going to be a day where a lot of money gets spent.

With the salary cap surging to $104 million next season, the cost of acquiring talent is going up.

At the head of the 2026 free-agent class is a Hockey Hall of Fame-bound goaltender in Sergei Bobrovsky and a couple of experienced blueliners who finished last season together with the Anaheim Ducks: John Carlson and Jacob Trouba.

While several pending unrestricted free agents took themselves off the board by signing extensions in recent weeks and months, those that remain should reap the benefits of being desired in a limited marketplace.

As the market comes into focus, the big board is expanding to 100 names.

As always, players are ranked by how closely they demand watching, given their potential impact and the buzz around them.

(Note: Net ratings are for 2025-26 via The Athletic’s Dom Luszczyszyn’s model, stats are via Hockey-Reference and GSAx via Evolving-Hockey. Contract projections are via CapWages and AFP Analytics. Current contracts are listed with maximum average annual value after potential bonuses.)
